title: The wise men part 4
scripture_text: ‘’After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem and asked, “Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.” When King Herod heard this he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him. When he had called together all the people’s chief priests and teachers of the law, he asked them where the Messiah was to be born. “In Bethlehem in Judea,” they replied, “for this is what the prophet has written: “But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’’ Then Herod called the Magi secretly and found out from them the exact time the star had appeared. He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go and search carefully for the child. As soon as you find him, report to me, so that I too may go and worship him.” After they had heard the king, they went on their way, and the star they had seen when it rose, went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. When they saw the star, they were overjoyed. On coming to the house, they saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshipped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh. And having been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their country by another route.’’
devotional:
Their worship meant that they had to leave the darkness of the past. In all probability these men were involved in the dark crafts of the occult, so the journey they made to see Jesus was as much spiritual as it was geographical. There is one thing we can be certain about, if they had stayed where they where, they would have never worshiped Jesus. This was not an easy journey, geographically it was between 800-1000 miles. Spiritually, it was light years away.

4.Their worship meant they had the faith to humble themselves.

As they came into the house they saw Jesus. who was probably a toddler at the time, and they prostrated themselves before him. This was a holy moment, this was the greatest moment in the lives of these wise men, as they lay with their faces in the ground before the King of the universe embodied in the physical frame of a toddler.

5. Their worship was costly, or was it?

We know that they gave Jesus treasures of gold, frankincense and myrrh. We know that these are very costly, however, this kind of worship does not measure its giving in terms of cost, even if it is costly. This kind of worship thinks in terms of privilege not cost. Worship says, ‘Lord it is a totally undeserved honour and a wonderful privilege of life for me to bow in worship before you and give you all that I am and have.’

Let me draw your attention to one more group of people.

The leading priests and the teachers of the religious law.

I am inclined to think that these were the worst characters in our story. They were religious people who knew their scriptures, they knew God’s plans and God’s promises, and yet they had no heart for Jesus. As we know Jesus was born in Bethlehem about five miles from Jerusalem. However, we have no record of them going to find him or bowing down in worship before him.

I live in a country where lots of people are brought up in Christian homes, they are taught the scriptures, they go to church. They may profess to be Christian but if we could see inside their hearts we might discover that they are more like the religious leaders than like the wise men. They have no real desire for God, they really don’t grasp the wonder of worship, and maybe at times they are like Herod, feeling a bit threatened by Jesus. Hopefully this year we will be challenged by the Christmas story.
prayer: Father I pray that my religious practices will not keep me from authentic worship of you.
